div.head: Ger 18.2, 19
div.ab: [18.2] Fela sceal to holdan hames gerefan ⁊ to gemetfæstan manna hyrde. [19] Ic gecende be ðam ðe ic cuðe; se ðe bet cunne, gecyðe his mare.
fela sceal to holdan hames ge|refan . 7 to gemetfæstan manna hyrde . ic ge|cende be ðam ðe ic cuðe . se ðe bet cunne ge|cyðe his mare
Fela sceal to holdan hames gerefan and to gemetfæstan manna hyrde. [19] Ic gecende be ðam ðe ic cuðe; se ðe bet cunne, gecyðe his mare.
Viel gehört zum treuen Gutsamtmann und ordentlichen Menschenhirten. [19] Ich habe erklärt gemäss dem, was ich konnte [kannte]; wer besser kann [kennt], künde dessen mehr!
[18.2] Much belongs to a faithful estate-reeve and a well-ordered shepherd of men. [19] I have set out what I could [knew]; let him who can [knows] better make more of it known!
Many things are needed of a faithful reeve, and a responsible overseer of men. I have spoken about that which I know; he who knows better should make known more.
Many things are required of the trusty reeve of a homestead and of a responsible manager of people. [19] I have revealed what I know; let anyone who knows better make known more.
div.note: This row combines Liebermann's 18.2 and 19. ‘hyrdas folces’ is what Polity 12 calls the reeves. K: ‘holden’ corrected to ‘holdan’; spacing corrected. In another 12th-century hand there follows a list of ship-levies from the estates of the London church c. 1000. Liebermann compares Rect 21.1.
This row holds several of Rabin’s sections (18.2, 19), each marked with its number.
